meaning: Each tie names the phrase of the paper that a Lean declaration states, as read side by side for Proof Reader (wcook04/proof-reader 3858afbe00b2, papers/navier-stokes-library-12). Titles, reading notes, topics and comparisons are AI-drafted or AI-assessed; no mathematician has reviewed them.

families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).

notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.Internal.s: The statement is about Lean’s totalized second Fréchet derivative under C¹ regularity; it does not assert classical C² regularity.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsKeyField: The second derivative is the totalized Fréchet derivative of the first derivative.
The smoothness predicate in this file requires C¹ regularity with Lipschitz gradients on closed balls.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ScalarShape.Frac: The denominator is a natural number and may be zero until a later validity predicate imposes positivity.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.ScalarShape.FracEq: The raw cross-product relation is not transitive on all stored pairs: (1, 1) relates to (0, 0), which relates to (2, 1), while the first and last do not relate. Positive-denominator guards restore the intended interpretation as equality of rational quotients.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.SquareIntern: This is an energy inequality, with nonnegative unit-mass smoothing and local integrability assumptions.
notes.Breakdown.CertCell.headPotential: The pressure normalization subtracts the unit-ball average, fixing the additive constant.

(`prod_iter_fst`; [source](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StripTraceParts.lean#L764)).

ties.from: **The reversed test pairing separates.** Proved result. (`slice_pair_fst`; [source](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/StripTraceParts.lean#L769)).

ties.from: **Meridian orbit map preserves null sets.** Proved result. (`quasiMeasurePreserving_orbitPlane`; [source](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/TailAngularPlane.lean#L284)).

ties.from: **A sixth-power bound gives L6 membership.** Proved result. If f is measurable up to a null set, |f(y)|² ≤ B(y) everywhere and ∫B(y)³dy is finite, then f belongs to L⁶(R³). (`memLp_six_of`; [source](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/TailRayModes.lean#L346)).

ties.from: **Rectangle divergence boundary integrals.** Proved result. Let g:ℝ²→ℝ be globally C¹ and let W=(W₁,W₂) be C¹ on an open set U containing Q=[a₁,b₁]×[a₂,b₂], where a₁≤b₁ and a₂≤b₂. (`box_divergence`; [source](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/TailSquareSmooth.lean#L50)).

ties.from: **Weak upper and lower traces match.** Proved result. If h > 0 and f has weak derivative f′ on (−2h,2h), the upper and lower weak traces at zero computed using width h agree. ties.from: **Cauchy-Schwarz for square-root products.** Proved result. For almost-everywhere measurable nonnegative extended-valued functions, the integral of their square-root product is at most the product of the square roots of their integrals. (`lintegral_sqrt_mul_sqrt_le`; [source](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/TripleSlice.lean#L9)).

ties.from: **The three-slice product bound is proved.** Proved result. For three nonnegative measurable functions depending on the coordinate pairs, the triple integral of their square-root product is at most the square root of the product of their three planar integrals. (`tripleSliceBound`; [source](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/CertCell/TripleSlice.lean#L20)).
